  Number:  1055

  Base:    main
  Status:  open

  URL:     https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1055
  Assignees: alishakawaguchi
  Type:      task
  Created: 2026-08-14T17:33:40Z
  Updated: 2026-08-14T18:12:46Z

Description:
What was broken
Once the search service folds checkpoints into sessions (ENT-1595), legacy checkpoints — which have no session id — surface as session rows with an empty sessionId. The client dedup keyed on sessionId alone, so every one of those legacy sessions collapsed into a single row and all but one disappeared from results.
Why
The dedup assumed every session row carries a sessionId. That holds for modern sessions but not for legacy checkpoints folded server-side, whose only stable identity is their checkpoint id.
The fix
Dedupe by sessionId, falling back to checkpointId when sessionId is empty. Modern sessions are unaffected (they still key on sessionId); legacy folded sessions now each keep their own row.
Verified
Unit tests pass, including a new case covering folded legacy sessions with empty sessionId.

content.text:
Reviewed trail #1055 (`fix(search): dedupe folded legacy sessions by checkpointId`, ENT-1595, branch `ent-1595-client-dedup-fallback`, 3 commits, +66/-3). It builds clean and the search tests pass. But I ran the deduper directly on both `main` and the branch, and the headline finding is that **the bug described in the commit message doesn't exist in the code being changed.**

## 1. The stated mechanism is wrong (blocking — needs a re-check of the real symptom)

The description says the client dedup "keyed on sessionId alone, so every one of those legacy sessions collapsed into a single row and all but one disappeared." That can't happen. `dedupSemanticResults` (`cmd/entire/cli/search_v4.go:527`) short-circuits on an empty id:

```go
id := r.ResultID()
if id == "" {
    deduped = append(deduped, r)   // results without an id are ALWAYS kept
    continue
}
```

On `main`, `ResultID()` for a folded legacy session returns `""` (empty `SessionID` → `resultField` returns `""` → `rawString("id")` returns `""` because `rawFields` is only populated for untyped rows). I ran it against `main` with three legacy rows plus a genuine duplicate pair:

```
in=5 out=4 dupes=map[session:1]
kept: sessionID="" display="a"   ← all three legacy rows survive
kept: sessionID="" display="b"
kept: sessionID="" display="c"
kept: sessionID="s1" display="d"
```

So the direction of the actual defect is the opposite of the one described: legacy rows were never collapsed, they were **never deduped at all** — a repo mirrored across cells would double-report each legacy session. If someone reported legacy sessions genuinely missing from results, the cause is upstream (most likely the server-side fold) and this change won't fix it. Worth confirming the original symptom was reproduced and is verified gone end to end.

## 2. What the change does do — both good, just described wrong

Running the same probe on the branch:

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| two distinct legacy rows | 2 kept | 2 kept ✅ |
| same legacy row from two cells | 2 kept (dupe leaks) | 1 kept ✅ |

Plus `ResultID()` now returns a real id for legacy rows, so they stop showing a blank ID column in the TUI (`search_tui.go:1221`) and a blank `"id"` in the agent-facing compact JSON (`search_cmd.go:1050`). Both are real improvements — the commit message just needs to say so instead of the collapse story.

Minor: those rows now carry `type: "session"` with a *checkpoint* id. The documented drill-down is `entire checkpoint explain <id>`, so that happens to work, but `entire session info <id>` won't. One sentence in the field comment would save someone the confusion.

## 3. No test at the level where the bug was claimed

Both new tests (`search_test.go:416`, `search_test.go:431`) exercise `ResultID`/`DedupID` in isolation. A single test calling `dedupSemanticResults` with legacy rows would have caught the wrong premise immediately — and it's the behavior that actually matters. I'd add it; I have the exact cases from the probe if useful.

## 4. The repo-qualification (commit 86659ea2d) is fragile in a way the tests don't cover

`DedupID` keys on `Org + "\x00" + Repo + "\x00" + CheckpointID` (`search/search.go:388`). That makes cross-cell dedup depend on two more fields agreeing exactly across cells. Measured on the branch:

```
legacy row, org/repo missing on one cell   in=2 out=2  ← dupe leaks
legacy row, casing skew across cells       in=2 out=2  ← dupe leaks
one cell lacks checkpointId (older cell)   in=2 out=2  ← dupe leaks
```

The casing case isn't hypothetical in this codebase — `resolveRepoFilters` (`search_cmd.go:597-600`) lowercases `FullName` precisely because "casing differences between the git remote (e.g. entireio/CLI) and the repo index (entireio/cli)" occur. At minimum `strings.ToLower` both components. Severity is low (both cells read the same control plane, so they'll usually agree), but it's free to harden.

## 5. Checkpoint rows still use the unqualified id

If checkpoint ids are "unique only WITHIN a repo" — the justification in the `DedupID` comment — then `TypeCheckpoint` rows have the identical hole, since they key on raw `c.ID`. Confirmed on the branch:

```
checkpoint rows, same id in two repos   in=2 out=1 dupes=map[checkpoint:1]   ← one silently dropped
```

Legacy checkpoint ids are 6 random bytes (`checkpoint/id/id.go:166`), so the collision space is only 2⁴⁸ — the same premise that motivated commit 2. In practice the two colliding rows also have to land in the same result page, so real-world probability is negligible either way; the point is that the codebase should pick one policy rather than qualify sessions and not checkpoints. Either apply it to both or drop commit 2. (If the server's synthetic session key is itself repo-qualified, mirroring it is the right call — I can't see the BFF from here, so that's worth stating explicitly in the comment.)

## 6. Stale comments after commit 2

Both `SessionResult.CheckpointID` (`search/search.go:121-124`) and `TestResultID_SessionFallsBackToCheckpointID` (`search_test.go:412-415`) say "the cross-cell dedupe (ResultID) falls back to it". Commit 86659ea2d moved the dedupe to `DedupID`; `ResultID` is now display-only. Small, but these were written to explain exactly the thing that changed.

Using the API changes the picture materially. I queried the live search service directly.

## The fix is inert against the real wire format (blocking)

The CLI added:

```go
CheckpointID   string  `json:"checkpointId,omitempty"`
```

The search service does not emit `checkpointId`. It emits **`matchedCheckpointId`**. Across 918 session rows from 10 queries in the US cell, plus direct checks in both jurisdictions:

```
n=918   empty_sessionId=0   has_checkpointId=0   has_matchedCheckpointId=918
us: n=100  has_checkpointId=0  has_matched=100
eu: n=19   has_checkpointId=0  has_matched=19
```

A real API row decoded through the branch code, with `sessionId` cleared to simulate a folded row:

```
PROBE folded: sessionID="" CheckpointID="" ResultID="" DedupID=""
```

Identical to pre-fix behavior. `CheckpointID` never populates, so `ResultID`'s fallback and `DedupID`'s session branch are both unreachable — the blank id in the TUI and compact JSON is still blank, and legacy rows still aren't deduped. `git grep matchedCheckpointId` across the CLI returns nothing, so this field has never been modeled anywhere in the client.

Either the tag should be `matchedCheckpointId`, or the CLI is written against an ENT-1595 server contract that hasn't shipped yet. That needs confirming with whoever owns the server side. Worth noting `matchedCheckpointId` is present on *every* session row, not just legacy ones — so simply correcting the tag is safe: the fallback only fires when `sessionId` is empty, and the existing tests still hold.

One semantic caveat if the tag is corrected: `matchedCheckpointId` is the checkpoint that *matched this query*, not a stable session identity. It's fine for cross-cell dedup of a single query (both cells run the same query against identical mirror content), but it means a legacy row's displayed id varies by search term. Probably acceptable; worth being deliberate about.

## The premise is unobserved on live data

No session row in either jurisdiction has an empty `sessionId` — 0 of 918. So the server-side fold either isn't deployed yet or always populates `sessionId`. The description's "Verified" section is entirely synthetic fixtures; nothing has been exercised against a real folded row, because none exist yet. The commit message says `checkpointId` "only exists in the unmerged fold PR." That's the part I can't see from here, and it's exactly the ordering hazard:

```
fold w/ checkpointId only: Matched="" ResultID="" DedupID=""
```

If the server-side fold merges emitting `checkpointId` for folded rows — the name it uses today, per your own commit message — the CLI goes inert again for precisely the rows this feature exists to handle, and the failure is silent (blank ids, no dedup, no error). Accepting both names removes the cross-repo merge-ordering dependency for about three lines — a `checkpointId` alias read in `UnmarshalJSON`, or a second field consulted as a fallback. Worth it given the two repos merge independently and nothing fails loudly if the assumption breaks. If the fold PR is already being updated to `matchedCheckpointId`, then this is a non-issue and only worth a sentence in the comment recording that the two names were reconciled deliberately.
